message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory protections and responsibilities under the Texas Property Code and related laws. Below is an overview of key rights you typically enjoy as a renter: | Category | Typical Rights (and some responsibilities) | |----------|-------------------------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit and two months’ rent for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep premises safe, sanitary, and structurally sound.
• Must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, and other essential services. | | **Repair & Maintenance** | • If landlord fails to repair, you may withhold rent (after giving written notice), or pay yourself and deduct from rent.
• In extreme cases, you can sue for damages if repairs are not made. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter without reasonable notice (usually 24 hours) except in emergencies. | | **Lease Terms** | • Written leases are required for residential rentals over 12 months.
• Lease terms must comply with state law; illegal clauses (e.g., waiving your right to sue) are unenforceable. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must give proper notice (30 days for nonpayment, 90 days for lease violations).
• Eviction requires court action; landlords cannot forcibly remove you. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Fair Housing Act prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, family status, etc. | | **Rent Control** | • Texas has no statewide rent control; however, local ordinances may apply in certain cities. | | **Utilities** | • Tenants usually responsible for utilities unless otherwise specified in lease. | | **Subletting / Assignment** | • Generally allowed with landlord’s consent; lease may restrict it. | | **Insurance** | • Landlord must carry insurance covering property damage; tenants often need renters’ insurance for personal belongings. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Read the Lease Carefully** – Ensure all promises (repairs, deposit return, pet policies) are documented. 2. **Document Issues** – Take photos, keep records of communication with landlord. 3. **Give Written Notice** – For repairs or complaints, send a certified letter or email. 4. **Know the Timeline** – Understand how long a landlord has to respond or complete repairs. 5. **Seek Legal Aid** – If disputes arise, consult a local attorney or tenant advocacy group. --- If you’d like a sample lease or a more detailed explanation tailored to a particular situation (e.g., furnished vs. unfurnished, short‑term rental, etc.), let me know!
